notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0527.tlg021.1st1K-gr: The text reads ἐπορεύθην, "I went"; the sense seems to want "he went", since it is Ahikar, not the blinded speaker, who would go to Elymais.

Esarhaddon is Σαχερδονός (Sacherdonos) in the Greek. υἱὸς ἐκ δευτέρας is awkward: υἱός ("son") seems to describe Esarhaddon as the previous king's son, and ἐκ δευτέρας may mean "a second time" or "as second [in rank]". ἐξάδελφος is taken as "nephew", since the preceding verse makes Ahikar the son of the speaker's brother.
The vertical bar in 6.16 stands in the source text and is kept in place.

nodes.text: And Ahikar interceded for me, and I came to Nineveh. Now Ahikar was the cupbearer and keeper of the signet, and administrator and accountant, and Esarhaddon, [the] son, appointed him a second time; and he was my nephew.

And I did not know that there were sparrows in the wall; and as my eyes were open, the sparrows dropped warm dung into my eyes, and white films formed on my eyes; and I went to physicians, and they did not help me. And Ahikar supported me until I went to Elymais.

because she had been given to seven husbands, and Asmodeus, the evil *daimonion* [demon], had killed them before they had been with her as [is the way] with wives. (9) And they said to her, "Do you not understand that you are strangling your husbands? You have already had seven, and you have had no joy of even one of them."
And he went to look for a man, and he found Raphael, who was an angel, and he did not know [it];

And he said to him, "The heart and the liver: if a *daimonion* [demon] or an evil spirit troubles anyone, these are to be burned as smoke before a man or a woman, and he will never be troubled again."

And now I am my father's only [son], and I am afraid that if I go in I will die as the earlier ones did, because a *daimonion* [demon] loves her, which harms no one except those who come near her. And now I am afraid that I will die, and bring my father's and my mother's life down to their grave in grief over me; and they have no other son who will bury them.

But the angel said to him, "Do you not remember the words your father commanded you, that you should take a wife from your own kin? And now listen to me, brother, | for she will be your wife; and pay no heed to the *daimonion*, for this night she will be given to you as wife.
And when you go into the bridal chamber, you will take ashes of incense and put on [them some] of the heart and the liver of the fish, and you will make smoke,

and the *daimonion* will smell it and flee, and will not come back for ever and ever. And when you go to her, rise up, both of you, and cry out to the merciful God, and he will save you and have mercy. Do not be afraid, for she was prepared for you from eternity, and you will save her, and she will go with you, and I suppose that you will have children by her." And when Tobias heard these things, he loved her, and his soul clung to her greatly.
And when the *daimonion* [demon] smelled the odour, it fled to the uppermost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound it.
I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who bring up the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.
